implementation_notes: The dominant Java realisation: the entity is a plain class with private fields, ordinary accessors and a no-arg constructor, annotated with @Entity/@Table/@Column/@Id/@GeneratedValue; the provider (Hibernate, EclipseLink) reads the annotations at bootstrap, builds the metamodel and generates SQL, while EntityManager and transactions stay outside the class. The annotations carry the mapping metadata and the entity has no save/load methods - the provider's generated mapper and persistence context replace the classic hand-written mapping code. Choose orm.xml only when the class must stay annotation-free.
pitfalls: Annotations only take effect inside a configured persistence unit; the same class outside one is just a POJO and nothing maps it.
Providers need non-final classes and a no-arg constructor for proxies (lazy loading, dirty checking) - final entities and field-only construction break them subtly.
equals/hashCode built on a generated id change value after persist; prefer a business key or an assigned-id convention.

variants.name: External JPA mapping files (orm.xml)
variants.implementation_notes: Classic externalised variant: the entity carries no annotations at all and the mapping lives in META-INF/orm.xml, which the provider merges with and overrides annotation defaults; schemas can be retargeted per deployment without recompiling the domain model. Prefer it where one model must map to different schemas or where domain code must not import a persistence package.
variants.code_sketch:
<entity-mappings version="2.1"
    xmlns="http://xmlns.jcp.org/xml/ns/persistence/orm">
  <entity class="com.example.User">
    <table name="users"/>
    <attributes>
      <id name="id"><column name="id"/></id>
      <basic name="email"><column name="email_address"/></basic>
    </attributes>
  </entity>
</entity-mappings>
pitfalls: The XML is not checked by the compiler: a renamed field breaks at bootstrap with a mapping exception.
Annotation defaults still apply where orm.xml is silent, so mixed metadata produces surprising effective mappings.
